about.headline:
Not an event.
12 hours of building.
about.paragraph1: The Next Craft is the in-person hackathon by Crafter Station × Next. 12 hours of real work, running simultaneously in Lima, Bogotá, Guatemala, Arequipa and El Salvador, with 300 hackers solving real problems.
about.paragraph2: Admission is selective. No room for spectators, no space for pretty slides. You come to ship real product: with users, with data, with something that works when the clock runs out.

place.label: PLACE
place.value: Lima · Bogotá · Guatemala · Arequipa · El Salvador

tracks.label: TRACKS
tracks.headline:
3 TRACKS.
PICK YOUR WEAPON.
tracks.intro: The bar is still one: what you build has to be used by someone real before the bell rings.

items.name: CONTENT MACHINE
items.desc: Build tools that create, edit, publish or distribute content — designed as a real product, not a demo. Something people actually use and that runs on its own.
ideas: An assistant that turns your work into content and publishes it for you
Long-form → clips, picking the best moments instead of random cuts
A tool that repurposes your old content in a smart way
Publish to several platforms at once, without it breaking
Not just generating content: measuring whether it actually lands
items.why: This is how products grow today. The challenge is making it work for real and at scale, not just in the demo.

items.name: OUT OF THE BOX
items.desc: Build something weird, experimental or unclassifiable — but with a technical spark. Real-time, novel interfaces, generative, hardware. The rule: make people react.
ideas: A voice interface that responds instantly
Something generative and live that reacts to whoever uses it
A game with characters that actually think
Something that mixes hardware or sensors with AI
An extension that does something unexpected with the page
A 'joke but useful' app with a good trick behind it
items.why: Viral projects come from here. Permission to experiment instead of building another SaaS — but done well.

items.name: LEARNING BY SHIPPING
items.desc: Build tools to learn by doing: that adapt, give real feedback and evaluate your work. No passive education — the product has to make you do.
ideas: A tutor that teaches with projects and gives you real feedback
Feedback that adapts to what you already know and what you're missing
Practice that adjusts to what you tend to forget
Practice interviews that actually evaluate you
An environment that runs and tests your code while you learn
Mentor matching that connects the right people
items.why: The education track, but with a better angle: less school, more doing.

events.description: Mentorship with Next Fellow and Crafter Station
Demos — 3 minutes per team, live product

prizes.label: PRIZES
perks: Access to the Crafter Station community
1,000 Tavily credits (8 USD in partner credits)
50 USD in Vapi credits per participant
prizes.winnersAria: Partner credit prizes for the top three winning teams
prizes.note: Jury evaluates with live demo + pitch. We'll publish the rubric soon.

items.question: Who can apply?
items.answer: Anyone who builds: devs, designers, PMs. Admission is selective: what you've shipped matters, not your résumé.

items.question: Can I apply without a team?
items.answer: Yes. Team formation happens at the kickoff. Teams of 3 to 5.

items.question: What should I bring?
items.answer: Laptop, charger and energy. Food, coffee and power are on us.

items.question: Can I use AI?
items.answer: Yes, you can use AI. But the code must be built during the hackathon — no pre-existing code will be accepted.

items.question: Who owns the IP?
items.answer: You do. 100%. We just want to watch you ship.

items.question: Is it in-person?
items.answer: Yes, it'll be in-person in Lima, Bogotá, Guatemala, Arequipa or El Salvador — whichever hub fits you. No remote option.

items.question: How does the jury evaluate?
items.answer: Live demo + pitch. We'll publish the rubric soon.
